A_axis: floral attractive/reward traits: corolla length; pollen; nectar; volatile classes
candidate_cost_evidence: Pearson correlations between defensive and attractive/reward traits as an explicit allocation-tradeoff test
result: No correlations between leaf or floral cucurbitacins and any floral attractive/reward trait; |r|<0.25 and P>0.05 for all
reason: The authors explicitly test an allocation-tradeoff prediction, but trait covariance is not a measurement of construction/allocation cost. A null covariance cannot be interpreted as kappa=0.

unit_linkage: individual within populations for floral/foliar volatiles; population-level alignment used where glucosinolate individuals differ
result: Between-group integration was low: floral scent-foliar volatile index 4.18; floral scent-glucosinolate index 4.24; no strong negative correlations among groups
reason: The study tests evolutionary integration rather than resource expenditure. The D axes are foliar rather than flower-specific, and low integration means evolutionary independence, not absence of a direct joint construction cost.

candidate_cost_evidence: association of colour morph and constitutive/induced secondary chemistry; possible pleiotropy or tight linkage discussed
result: Petal colour morph is associated with aspects of inducibility/secondary chemistry architecture, but no direct resource or construction-cost variable and no A x D allocation term is measured
reason: Genetic linkage or pleiotropy can generate trait covariance without an energetic allocation cost. This study therefore cannot identify kappa.

A_axis: petal size; floral display; pollinator reward/use proxies
D_axis: artificially selected high versus low myrosinase herbivore resistance
candidate_cost_evidence: ecological cost of resistance expressed through altered floral traits and pollinator foraging
result: High-resistance plants developed smaller petals later in life; floral display also depended on resistance x damage; pollinators spent more time per flower on low-resistance plants while total pollinator attraction did not differ
reason: The paper deliberately studies an ecological cost of resistance in the currency of pollination. That maps to defence effects on mutualist use / floral phenotype, not to a measured resource term depending jointly on an attraction trait and flower-specific D. Labeling every 'cost of resistance' as kappa would confound iota-like ecological interference with direct allocation/construction cost.
